ring_observation.conclusion: with 0x66F20E neutralised, 0x5B2C10 does not emit any loopback packet; there is no challenge to answer

answers.question: how many times does CL_Init run during one 0x5B2C10 call
answers.answer: zero inside 0x5B2C10. CL_Init is not called by 0x5B2C10; it is called once by 0x4FE740 (return address 0x4FE780) immediately after phase is forced to 8, together with one CL_Shutdown (return address 0x4FE779). 0x5B2C10 itself is called twice per phase-8 attempt by the heartbeat path 0x5C2AED -> 0x5B3160 (return address 0x5B31B9).

findings.finding: 0x4FE740 is the reset routine: CL_Shutdown() then CL_Init(1). Its callers are 0x4FD98B and 0x5C0093. Forcing phase 8 reliably triggers it once per attempt; the object pair cl/cl2 is re-created (cl 0x13932A00 -> 0x13933600).

0x5B3160 (called from 0x5C2AED) is the per-frame client update: if [0x76446B0] >= 7 and != 0x0A and [0xC7AF6A8]-[cl+8] >= 0x1F4 ms, it calls 0x5B2B70 and then 0x5B2C10. Therefore phase >= 7 makes the client retry the connection initialiser every 500 ms. The old conclusion 'the frame tick never calls 0x5B2C10' was produced with the 9-byte entry stub in place and is contradicted by this measurement.

[0x76446B0]=8 is not a legal client phase. 0x77C290's tail at 0x77C343 writes 0 unconditionally unless phase == 5 (when cl != 0). The legitimate phase values written by the shipped code are 3 (0x470467), 4 (0x5BEA8B), 5, 7 (0x5BE90A and 0x813D34). The 8 used in earlier rounds is why every attempt is torn down 1-3 s later.

0x66F170 decodes its callback as (cl2+0x2C) ^ [cl2+0x30] ^ [0xE60B78] and calls it. In every measured state cl2+0x2C and [cl2+0x30] are zero, while [0xE60B78] changes per process (0xBBF195E1 in session 2), so the call target is a different garbage address each run. Session 1 crashed at exactly that target with eax=cl2+0x1C and edi=cl2+0xC, confirming the decode site.

The cl2 object is fully initialised where previous rounds expected it to be broken: cl2+0xA8F0 holds an encoded pointer (0x852AF411 etc.), cl2+0xA8DC is 0x1F and cl2+0xA8D8 is 0x20. The missing piece is only the callback object at cl2+0x1C..0x30, which is all zero.

Even when 0x5B2C10 runs (twice) without crashing, ring A and ring B stay at cursor 0 and cl+0x14 (connection netadr) stays all zero, so the initialiser produces no outbound packet. This explains why the phase is torn down: there is nothing to answer.

next: use phase 7 (or the official sequence at 0x813D11: CL_Shutdown; CL_Init(3 or 7); [0x76446B0]=7) instead of the illegal phase 8
initialise cl2+0x1C..0x30 by finding the shipped writer, or redirect the decoded callback to a controlled stub to learn its contract
make 0x5B2C10 emit a packet: either provide the callback object or drive the older CL_Connect path with a loopback netadr written into the rebuilt cl
do not repair cl+0xA8F0 again; the field belongs to cl2 and is already valid
